Extend the hub across Salesforce and Jira

Intermediate 60 minutes Lab 2 of 3
Introduction
  1. A call comes in
    CyberCore Technologies is on the line. Their account history is in Salesforce, the open bug is a Jira ticket, the resolution steps are a Confluence SOP.
    01
  2. The app-switching tax
    Working the call means three tabs, three logins, and copy-paste between them. The agent assembles the picture by hand while the customer waits.
    02
  3. One conversation
    The AI client reads all three systems, finds the open request, and recommends next steps grounded in the SOPs — in a single thread.

In this lab, you'll act as integration engineer for IDEA Brands — extending Maya's MCP server across Salesforce and Jira so her AI client can work a full customer issue without switching tabs. The lab data is synthetic and intentionally messy.

MO
Maya Okonkwo
Tier-1 Support Agent · IDEA Brands

One call touches three systems. The customer's account is in Salesforce, their bug is in Jira, the fix is in Confluence.

The question

Can one AI client reason across Salesforce, Jira, and Confluence to work a single customer issue end to end?

You'll learn how to

  • Update the server instructions for a multi-application scope
  • Add six Salesforce and Jira tools to the existing MCP server
  • Curate the tool set with clearer descriptions and fewer overlaps
  • Run cross-system prompts and watch the AI client reason across tools
  • Inspect job history and logs to see exactly which tools ran

What you'll need

  • The Customer Support Hub MCP server from Lab 1, connected to LibreChat
  • Your ATT##_MCP project, which already contains six Salesforce and Jira tools
  • Familiarity with reading a Workato recipe (Foundations 1 or equivalent) — you'll step through job history in Phase 2
Phase 1

Extend the hub across systems

Can one server speak Salesforce and Jira as well as Confluence?

Pattern

Cross-functional tool collection

A business task rarely lives in one system. Extending the server with Salesforce (accounts, cases) and Jira (engineering tickets) turns a documentation assistant into a support assistant. The skill is curation: adding the right tools, describing them precisely, and removing the ones that overlap or distract.

1.1

Re-scope the server instructions

Your server now does more than read docs — it'll touch customer accounts and engineering tickets. The server instructions have to say so, or the model keeps treating it as a Confluence-only assistant. Re-scope them first.

Overview

Download the Lab 2 instructions from FileStorage (Tools > FileStorage > /Lab Assets/MCP-2/mcp-ex2-server-instructions.md). On your Customer Support Hub server's Overview tab, edit Server instruction and replace the Lab 1 text with the new multi-app version.

Apply these values
FieldValue
FileStorage path/Lab Assets/MCP-2/mcp-ex2-server-instructions.md
TargetServer Overview → Server instruction
ActionReplace Lab 1 instructions, save
Detailed steps 4 steps

The instructions are read by the LLM, not the person in chat. Broadening them — "this server spans Confluence, Salesforce, and Jira; always search before answering; confirm before writing" — is what makes the model consider the new tools at all.

  • Open Tools > FileStorage and navigate to /Lab Assets/MCP-2/.
  • Download mcp-ex2-server-instructions.md.
  • Open your Customer Support Hub server and, on the Overview tab, click Edit on Server instruction.
  • Replace the existing text with the Lab 2 instructions and save.
Verify the Server instruction describes a multi-system support assistant spanning Confluence, Salesforce, and Jira.
1.2

Add the cross-system tools

Your project already contains six multi-application tools wired to Salesforce and Jira — account lookups, support requests, comments. They are not on the server yet. Add them to the Customer Support Hub you built in Lab 1.

Overview

On the server's Overview tab, find the Tools section and click Add tools. Choose Add from this project, select all six available Salesforce and Jira tools, and click Add tools.

Apply these values
FieldValue
SectionServer Overview → Tools
ActionAdd tools → Add from this project
SelectionAll 6 Salesforce / Jira tools
Examplesget_account_info, search_accounts, create_support_request, get_support_request_details, add_support_request_comments, search_support_requests
Detailed steps 4 steps

These tools are pre-built recipes exposed as MCP functions. Adding them is what gives the AI client a way to act in Salesforce and Jira, not only read Confluence.

  • On the server Overview tab, locate the Tools section and click Add tools.
  • Choose Add from this project.
  • Select all the available tools (tick the project checkbox to select the whole set).
  • Click Add tools.
Verify all six Salesforce and Jira tools appear in the server's Tools list alongside the Confluence ones.
1.3

Curate the tool set

More tools isn't better. Two of the template's Confluence tools — archiving and label-deletion — aren't part of a support workflow and only give the model wrong turns to take. And one new tool, get_account_info, needs a description that says when not to use it. Curate.

Overview

Edit the get_account_info tool and give it a description that draws the line against search_accounts. Then remove the two Confluence tools you don't need: archive_page and delete_label.

Note

search vs get

search_accounts finds an account when you only have a name; get_account_info pulls the full picture once you have an ID. They look similar and the model will confuse them unless the descriptions say which is which — and which to reach for first. That's the whole point of a good description.

Apply these values
ToolAction
get_account_infoAdd description (below)
archive_pageRemove from server
delete_labelRemove from server
Detailed steps 4 steps

Curation is the real move here: one sharper description so the model stops confusing get_account_info with search_accounts, and two fewer tools so it has fewer wrong turns to take. Both are design decisions, not busywork.

  • In the Tools list, find get_account_info and click the pencil to Edit tool description.
  • Set the description to: Retrieve comprehensive information about a customer account including contacts, open support requests, and opportunities. Use when you have an account ID and need the complete picture of the customer relationship. When NOT to use: if searching for an account by name, use search_accounts first to get the account ID.
  • Save the description.
  • In the Tools list, select archive_page and delete_label and choose Remove tools.
Verify the Tools list shows the curated set: get_account_info carries its new description, and archive_page and delete_label are gone.
1.4

Force the client to re-fetch

You changed the server, but LibreChat is holding a cached copy of its tools and instructions. Until you reconnect, it's reasoning over yesterday's server. Force a re-fetch.

Overview

In LibreChat, open MCP Settings from the left sidebar, find YourName MCP in your server list, and reconnect it. That pulls the latest tools and instructions from your server.

Heads up

Do this every time you change the server — new tools, edited descriptions, updated instructions. When a change doesn't show up in chat, check the reconnect first.

Apply these values
FieldValue
PathLibreChat → MCP Settings → YourName MCP
ActionReconnect the server
Detailed steps 4 steps

The client caches the server's surface for speed. Reconnecting is the explicit "re-read the contract" action — make it muscle memory for the rest of the lab.

  • In LibreChat, open MCP Settings from the left sidebar.
  • Find YourName MCP in your server list.
  • Reconnect the server so LibreChat re-fetches its tools and instructions.
  • Start a new chat and select the server so the conversation uses the refreshed surface.
Verify asking the server what it can do now lists the Salesforce and Jira capabilities, not only Confluence.
Phase 2

Reason across systems

Will the AI client chain the right tools across apps on its own?

Pattern

Multi-tool reasoning

Given one natural-language request, the client decides which tools to call, in what order, passing outputs between them — search an account, find its open case, write an update. You don't script the chain; the model plans it from your tool descriptions. The job report and logs are how you see the plan it actually ran.

2.1

Run a cross-system request

Here's the payoff. One plain-English request — find a customer's open case and update it — should make the AI client search Salesforce for the account, find the open request, and write a comment, all in one turn. You don't script the chain; the model plans it.

Overview

In a fresh, MCP-attached chat, prompt: I'm on with CyberCore Technologies. Find their open request and add an update stating it's starting to affect their revenue. Watch the plan it builds — typically an account search, a request lookup, then a comment write. The exact tools vary because the model plans the chain; the job report in the next task shows the chain it actually ran. If you have time, try the harder prompts below — each is a multi-minute chain, so treat them as optional.

Try these
PromptWhat it exercises
I'm on with CyberCore Technologies. Find their open request and add an update stating it's starting to affect their revenue.account search → request lookup → comment write
Pull DataStream Analytics, Quantum Innovations, and CyberCore Technologies support requests. Recommend a prioritization based on our SOPs.multi-account + Confluence
Find all Synergy Technologies cases, link me to the SOP that best matches each issue, and suggest next steps.cross-system synthesis
Look at the current requests for Prism Technologies and tell me which docs would be most useful.case → doc match
Detailed steps 4 steps

This is multi-tool reasoning: the client passes the account it found into the case lookup, then into the comment write — a plan built from your tool descriptions, which is why Lab 3 exists.

  • Start a new chat and select YourName MCP (a fresh context avoids priming).
  • Send the CyberCore prompt above.
  • Watch the tool calls: an account search, a request lookup, then a comment write.
  • Hold off on the harder prompts for now — read the evidence for the chain you triggered in the next two tasks first, then come back and explore.
Verify LibreChat finds CyberCore's open request and posts your revenue-impact comment — you'll confirm it end to end in the job report in the next task.
2.2

See what the tool actually did

The chat shows you the answer; the job report shows you the work. Every tool call is a recipe job you can open, step through, and inspect — inputs, outputs, the data that moved between systems.

Overview

Back in Workato, open the Customer Support Hub folder and click a tool's skill (for example search_pages) to see its Jobs. Open a recent job and step through it — toggle step inputs and outputs, and use Expand data to see the full payloads.

Apply these values
FieldValue
LocationATT##_MCP → Customer Support Hub folder
OpenA tool skill (e.g. search_pages) → Jobs
InspectA recent job → step inputs/outputs → Expand data
Detailed steps 5 steps

The job report is your ground truth. When the chat's answer is surprising, this is where you confirm what the tool actually received and returned — before you blame the model.

  • In your project, open the Customer Support Hub folder.
  • Click a tool skill such as search_pages to view its Jobs.
  • Open a recent job from the list.
  • Click individual steps and toggle their inputs and outputs.
  • Use Expand data to see the full request and response payloads.
Verify you can point to the exact input a tool received and the exact output it returned for a call you triggered from LibreChat.
2.3

Trace a call through the logs

Job reports show one recipe's runs. Logs show every MCP call across the server — the system of record for compliance, analytics, and alerting. Learn to filter them to the call you care about.

Overview

From the job report, click View log entries. The logs open pre-filtered to that Job ID. Clear the Job ID filter and filter by Recipe ID instead to see the broader picture. Logs can stream to external destinations for retention and monitoring.

Apply these values
FieldValue
Entry pointJob report → View log entries
Default filterJob ID (one call)
BroadenClear Job ID, filter by Recipe ID
Detailed steps 4 steps

Logs are the durable, exportable record. In production they're streamed off-platform; here, learn the filter moves — Job ID for one call, Recipe ID for the tool's whole history.

  • In an open job report, click View log entries on the right.
  • Note the logs default to a filter for that specific Job ID.
  • Clear the Job ID filter and add a Recipe ID filter to see all calls for that tool.
  • Read a log entry's message_type and payload to see the tool call recorded end to end.
Verify you can switch between a single-call view (Job ID) and a whole-tool view (Recipe ID) and read the tool_call log entries.

Reflect

Now that the server spans three systems, consider what the evidence trail changes about how you'd run this for real users.

  • The cross-system chain wasn't scripted — the model planned it. What in your server made that plan reliable, and what made it fragile?
  • A teammate edits a tool description, re-asks their prompt in the same chat, and sees no change. Walk through what actually happened — and where the fix lives.
  • A teammate suggests exposing twenty more tools to "cover every case." Using what you saw in the job report and logs, argue for a smaller, sharper set.

Wrap-up

Maya works the CyberCore call in one thread. The AI client searches Salesforce for the account, opens the Jira-backed request, posts the revenue-impact update, and points her to the matching SOP — no tab-switching, no copy-paste. Every step of that chain is on the record, in the job report and the logs.

Patterns to carry forward:

  • A business task spans systems; so should the server. You watched one server carry a three-system call in a single thread — curate it across apps rather than juggling many narrow ones.
  • Curation is design. Removing an overlapping tool and sharpening a description improves accuracy as much as adding a capability.
  • The evidence is a layer below the chat. Job reports and logs show what one prompt actually ran — debug and audit from them, not from the answer.

When the client surprises you, prompt it to explain its tool-selection reasoning and suggest description changes. In Lab 3 you make those changes the durable fix — tuning the tool contract itself.

Appendix · Using Claude instead of LibreChat

The training environment uses LibreChat, but any MCP-capable client works the same way. To connect this server to Claude: open Customize > Connectors, click the + and choose Add custom connector, then paste the same Developer MCP Token URL. Start a chat and ask What can YourName MCP do?.

Bonus challenges

Still have time? Two ways to push the server further before Lab 3 tunes the contract.

  • Connect the same server to Claude (see the appendix) and run one of the cross-system prompts. Check whether the tool selection matches LibreChat.
  • Using the job report and logs, trace one multi-tool prompt end to end and find the slowest tool — the first thing you'd optimize in production.
